edition.notes: The Garnier reprint of Migne's volume 16, read on its own title page (leaf 5 of the Internet Archive scan patrologiaecur16mign): PATROLOGIAE LATINAE TOMUS XVI, S. AMBROSIUS, PARISIIS, APUD GARNIER FRATRES, EDITORES ET J.-P. MIGNE SUCCESSORES, 1880. Migne reprints the Maurist edition of De sacramentis together with the Maurist admonitio and variant notes; those notes record that the reading ratam at IV, 5, 21 was absent from all earlier printings and some manuscripts and is restored from several others. Column numbering, not the leaf numbering of the scan, is the citation grammar. The authenticity of De sacramentis as Ambrose's own preaching was long disputed and the Maurist apparatus printed here preserves that dispute; twentieth-century scholarship generally reversed the earlier doubt, and this record takes no position beyond what the inspected pages show.

passages.context: Ambrose (or the author of De sacramentis) IV, 5, 21, read visually at column 462: 'Vis scire quia verbis coelestibus consecratur? Accipe quae sunt verba. Dicit sacerdos: Fac nobis, inquit, hanc oblationem ascriptam, ratam, rationabilem, acceptabilem: quod figura est corporis et [sanguinis Domini nostri Jesu Christi]', the sentence running over to column 463. The Maurist note 74 on the same column records that the word ratam was missing from all earlier editions and from some manuscripts and is restored from several others.
passages.notes: Read at the page image, not at raw OCR. The passage bears on the wording of the Roman Canon's Quam oblationem in the late fourth century; it does not establish that the surrounding Milanese eucharistic prayer is identical with the Roman Canon.

passages.context: De sacramentis IV, 5, 21-23 at column 463 ('Qui pridie quam pateretur, in sanctis manibus suis accepit panem, respexit in coelum ad te, sancte Pater omnipotens, aeterne Deus, gratias agens, benedixit, fregit, fractumque apostolis suis et discipulis suis tradidit, dicens: Accipite, et edite ex hoc omnes; hoc est enim corpus meum, quod pro multis confringetur', with the chalice narrative at IV, 5, 22) and IV, 6, 27 at column 464 ('Et sacerdos dicit: Ergo memores gloriosissimae ejus passionis, et ab inferis resurrectionis, et in coelum ascensionis, offerimus tibi hanc immaculatam hostiam, rationabilem hostiam, incruentam hostiam, hunc panem sanctum, et calicem vitae aeternae: et petimus et precamur, ut hanc oblationem suscipias in sublimi altari tuo per manus angelorum tuorum, sicut suscipere dignatus es munera pueri tui justi Abel, et sacrificium patriarchae nostri Abrahae, et quod tibi obtulit summus sacerdos Melchisedech'). Both columns were read visually.
passages.notes: The Maurist note 75 on the same leaf records that the words et discipulis suis are omitted in the Roman edition alone, and that where all editions and manuscripts read pro multis confringetur the same Roman edition corrected to pro vobis datur. The passage is a Milanese witness of the late fourth century; it establishes the antiquity of the pattern later fixed in the Roman Canon at Quam oblationem, Qui pridie, Unde et memores, Supra quae, and Supplices, not the identity of the two prayers.
